finding: Clinicea stores multiple before/after images from several angles and links them to each package and each treatment sitting, with a 'Compare Visits Visually' view.
our_action: Copy and go further: tie photos to Clinozy treatment sessions AND packages, add same-angle guides and side-by-side compare, and make it shareable on WhatsApp with the patient's consent.

finding: Reviewers rate Clinicea highly, with about 4.9/5 on Capterra across 16 to 31 reviews and almost no negative reviews. It sells itself as 'the most comprehensive Aesthetic Clinic management software'.
public_reaction: Mostly positive; one reviewer notes some users 'may find it a bit difficult during onboarding'.
our_action: Treat it as the benchmark for derma depth. Clinozy needs reviews early: seed Capterra and G2 with design-partner clinics before launch.

finding: A third-party India guide credits Clinicea with deep medical-derma features: body maps, Fitzpatrick skin type and isotretinoin tracking.
our_action: Gap check: Clinozy's brief lists prescriptions and photos but no body map, Fitzpatrick type or isotretinoin/teratogen monitoring. Add structured derma fields to the patient record.

finding: Clinicea exposes an API and has customisable branding, customisable reports and discount management (Software Advice feature list).
our_action: Clinozy has outbound webhooks only. Ship a documented public API and white-label patient-facing pages (booking and invoice links) with the clinic's brand.

finding: Reviewers ask for two-way WhatsApp, which suggests Clinicea's WhatsApp is one-way notifications at most.
public_reaction: "It would be better if they support 2-way Whatsapp Communication."
our_action: Lead with Clinozy's WhatsApp conversation inbox in Leads (Mine/Unreplied). Message: 'Reply to patients on WhatsApp inside the clinic software, not just send reminders.'

finding: Users have asked for an Android app.
public_reaction: "Clinicea should also indulge in created an android mobile app in the future. It will be beneficial for us."
our_action: Clinozy is a React PWA. Make it installable on Android and optimised for phones (doctor view, Today board), and market 'works on any phone, no download'.

finding: Reviewers say Clinicea's analytics and reports are hard to read and understand. The vendor replied that it is improving the Analytics module.
public_reaction: "Need to work on analytics for a better reporting view and understanding of reports."
our_action: Ship plain-language owner dashboards: revenue per doctor and machine, package liability, conversion from lead to patient, and a daily cash close summary on WhatsApp.

finding: Case sheets don't support nested or conditional forms, and voice and handwriting input were requested.
public_reaction: "The casesheets dont involve nested forms"; another wanted "voice support or touch support like writing on screen".
our_action: Build conditional, nested treatment and consult templates, plus voice dictation (an AI scribe) and stylus notes in Clinozy's patient record.

finding: Reviewers report friction: they can't open a patient profile from the calendar and can't fully delete a bill, with a bill-deletion issue reported in 2023.
public_reaction: "Bill delete was not able to do it completely."
our_action: Give every calendar card one click to the patient record. Handle invoice corrections as GST-compliant credit notes and voids with an audit trail, which Clinozy's audit log already supports.

finding: Some reviewers report delayed support on calls and a hard onboarding.
public_reaction: "Customer support response can sometimes be delayed on calls."
our_action: Offer WhatsApp-first support with a response-time promise and guided self-onboarding (import of patients and medicines, sample data).

finding: Clinicea charges per practitioner per month: Power $59, Premium $69, Enterprise $89, with a free trial and no free plan. An India guide estimates ₹1.2L–₹6L a year.
our_action: Price Clinozy per clinic or branch in INR (not per practitioner in USD) so adding a therapist or counsellor doesn't raise the bill. Show the saving next to Clinicea's per-seat cost.

finding: Before/after comparison tied to each package sitting makes progress visible.
psychology: Progress feedback (goal-gradient effect) keeps patients coming back for the next sitting. Visible results also justify the package price after purchase and reduce buyer's remorse.
our_action: Beat it: send the patient an automatic WhatsApp progress card after sitting 3 of 6 ('You're halfway there'), with the photo and a one-tap rebook. That turns photos into a retention habit loop, not just a record.

finding: Per-practitioner pricing makes adding staff feel like a recurring loss to owners.
psychology: Pain of paying: every new seat is a fresh, visible cost, so owners ration logins. That creates shared passwords and poor role data.
our_action: Use flat per-branch pricing with unlimited roles and message it as 'add your whole team free'. The endowment effect sets in once every staff member has their own login.

finding: HealthPlix sells AI-assisted EMR and fast prescribing ('Rx in 30 seconds'), with modules for 16 specialties and prescriptions in 14 languages.
our_action: Match prescription speed with derma favourites (one-tap acne/melasma regimens) and Hindi and regional-language printouts. Clinozy already has 11 UI languages, so extend them to prescriptions.

finding: Doctors send digital prescriptions by SMS or WhatsApp and can chat with patients on WhatsApp through a masked number, which keeps the doctor's personal number private.
our_action: Copy the masked-number idea. Route patient WhatsApp to a clinic number with assignment to staff, so doctors never share personal numbers. Make doctor privacy a selling point.

finding: HealthPlix claims to be India's largest doctor EMR, with over 15M patients treated through the platform.
our_action: You can't out-scale it on GP volume. Position Clinozy as the specialist for skin, hair and aesthetics, which a general EMR does not cover.

finding: Yearly plans start at ₹11,999 (Pro) and ₹17,999 (Elite) on Techjockey. ITQlick estimates about $200/month for one user. There is no free trial.
our_action: Benchmark: an entry-level Indian EMR costs ₹12–18k a year. Clinozy's full clinic suite can price above that, but offer a free trial since HealthPlix doesn't.

finding: AI-OCR and analytics are on higher tiers. HealthPlix uses AI to analyse a patient's history to support diagnosis.
our_action: Clinozy's brief has no AI. Add AI on top of what clinics already do: WhatsApp lead reply drafts, a consult scribe, and old paper-record OCR during onboarding.

finding: HealthPlix has a mobile EMR (SPOT) and a patient app that a G2 reviewer praised.
public_reaction: Five-star G2 review praised the patient app.
our_action: Clinozy has no patient-facing app. Ship a lightweight patient PWA or WhatsApp mini-flow for sessions left, invoices, photos and rebooking.

finding: HealthPlix has a G2 average of 2.8/5 from 3 reviews, with a March 2026 one-star review calling customer service 'very poor'.
public_reaction: "customer service very poor"
our_action: Comparison message: 'Real humans on WhatsApp, in your language.' Publish support response-time stats.

finding: A reviewer says the old local-language support staff could clear doubts quickly but now has to 'call the support team for every doubt'. Another rated support 1/5.
public_reaction: "Now they have to call the support team for every doubt."
our_action: Build in-app contextual help, the ⌘K palette with 'how do I…' answers, and an assigned onboarding manager for the first 30 days.

finding: Reviewers say pharmacy management needs improvement.
public_reaction: "Needs improvement in pharmacy management and updates required overall."
our_action: Clinozy's pharmacy module (batches, expiry, POs, MRs, credits) is a direct counter. Demo the dispense-from-prescription flow against HealthPlix.

finding: A review describes the product as 'Single Doctor use only', so multi-doctor clinics struggle.
public_reaction: "Single Doctor use only"
our_action: Target multi-doctor, multi-branch derma chains with Clinozy's roles (Therapist, Counsellor, Pharmacist), commissions and branch switching.

finding: HealthPlix is doctor-centric (prescriptions, EMR) with no room, machine, package or lead CRM for aesthetic procedures.
our_action: Position Clinozy as the whole clinic floor (laser and room bookings, counsellor, packages), not just the doctor's desk.

finding: 'Rx in 30 seconds' sells speed to time-starved OPD doctors.
psychology: Time-saving framing plus habit formation: once a doctor's personal templates and favourites are saved, switching costs (sunk effort) lock them in.
our_action: Beat it: import a doctor's existing HealthPlix or paper templates in onboarding so switching costs vanish, and show 'time saved today' on the doctor's dashboard.

finding: The masked WhatsApp number protects doctors' personal boundaries.
psychology: It speaks to doctors' status and identity and to autonomy: control over who reaches them reduces after-hours anxiety.
our_action: Message Clinozy as 'your patients reach the clinic, not your phone', with staff assignment, after-hours auto-replies and Unreplied views.

finding: MocDoc HMS is well rated: 4.9/5 from 44 reviews on Capterra, value-for-money 4.8, and 90% likely to recommend on GetApp.
public_reaction: Reviewers praise ease of use, billing speed and go-live help from the implementation team.
our_action: MocDoc wins on hand-held implementation. Clinozy needs an equally strong first-week setup.

finding: MocDoc sells a separate pharmacy module with batch tracking, expiry management, purchase orders and real-time inventory.
our_action: Clinozy already matches this. Include pharmacy in the core plan rather than as an add-on, to undercut MocDoc's modular pricing.

finding: MocDoc advertises GST-enabled receipts and invoices plus WhatsApp and SMS alerts for appointments and reports.
our_action: Table stakes in India. Clinozy must ship GST invoices on WhatsApp from launch.

finding: MocDoc covers the full spectrum from clinic to hospital (OPD/IPD) and labs, so clinics can grow into it.
our_action: Don't chase hospitals. Clinozy should own the aesthetic niche and add lab-report import or webhooks for derma labs.

finding: Reviewers ask for Tally reports. Tally export matters to Indian accountants.
public_reaction: "There some like tally report."
our_action: Build Tally export (XML/Excel) from Clinozy's payments ledger and pharmacy sales for the Accountant role.

finding: MocDoc's single-specialty page targets 'dermatology, cardiology, or pediatrics clinic' owners and says each specialty needs its own templates.
our_action: Clinozy should publish derma-specific landing pages and templates (acne, PRP, laser, hair transplant consent) to win specialty SEO.

finding: Pricing is quote-only with no free trial. A reviewer summary cites 'higher cost for add-on' and limited customisation in some modules.
public_reaction: "Limited customization options in certain modules and the higher cost for add-on"
our_action: Publish transparent INR pricing with all modules included and a self-serve trial. Message: 'No add-on surprises.'

finding: Integration and setup had challenges even for happy customers.
public_reaction: "The integration process was overall smooth, but there were some challenges that made it difficult."
our_action: Offer import wizards for patients, medicines and packages from Excel and other tools, so a clinic can go live the same day.

finding: Billing UX friction: the system asks for discount remarks when no discount was given, and there is no warning for unsaved work.
public_reaction: "It would be better if a warning message could appear when there is unsaved or partial work."
our_action: Use autosave drafts everywhere (checkout, prescriptions) and only ask for remarks when the lowest-price guard is triggered.

finding: MocDoc is hospital and lab heavy, with no lead CRM, package selling or before/after photos for aesthetics in its clinic marketing.
our_action: Message 'MocDoc runs hospitals; Clinozy grows aesthetic clinics': leads, packages, recalls and offers.

finding: Even minor complaints concern prescription aesthetics, such as asking for more colourful prescriptions.
public_reaction: "The prescription could be made more colourful."
our_action: Offer branded, well-designed prescription and invoice templates. For aesthetic clinics the printout is part of the brand.

finding: Hand-holding during go-live builds strong reciprocity and loyalty, which shows up in reviews.
psychology: Reciprocity and the 'IKEA effect': when a vendor co-builds the setup, the clinic feels it owns the system and rates it highly, which makes it sticky.
our_action: Beat it: run co-setup sessions in which the clinic configures its own packages and price list with a Clinozy specialist. Then ask for a review at the 'aha' moment, such as the first day-close.

finding: Quote-only, modular pricing anchors high and then discounts.
psychology: Anchoring and opacity: sales-led quotes create a 'deal' feeling but raise distrust and stall self-serve buyers.
our_action: Beat it: transparent price cards with a 'what MocDoc charges for add-ons' comparison. Transparency signals trust to small clinic owners.

finding: EkaScribe is an AI scribe that auto-generates prescriptions, symptom logs and histories from the consult. It is ABDM-compliant and can plug into other EMRs.
our_action: Clinozy has no AI scribe. Partner with one (EkaScribe-style) or build a consult-to-prescription AI tuned to derma and aesthetic vocabulary.

finding: Eka Care is the first private platform approved by ABDM to create ABHA cards and supports ABHA linking and longitudinal records.
our_action: Gap: Clinozy's brief has no ABDM/ABHA. Add ABHA linking and health-record sharing for compliance and government-scheme incentives.

finding: Eka Care reportedly integrates Google Reserve, WhatsApp, Razorpay, Google Meet and Flabs.
our_action: Add 'Book with Google' (Reserve) and Razorpay/UPI payment links. Stripe alone is weak for Indian patient payments.

finding: The doctor app is free on the App Store with a free account or 7-day trial. Paid plans: Eka Doc Plus ₹16,999/yr, Doc Pro ₹18,749/yr, Clinic Pro ₹1,00,000/yr.
our_action: Clinic Pro at ₹1L/yr is a useful anchor. Clinozy's full aesthetic suite can price near it with packages, pharmacy and CRM included.

finding: Eka Care claims 25,000+ doctors or 33K clinics and raised a $15M Series A.
our_action: Expect Eka to bundle aggressively. Compete on aesthetic workflows rather than on price.

finding: Eka runs a consumer PHR app alongside the doctor app, so patients hold their own records and the doctor stays in their pocket.
our_action: Give Clinozy patients a WhatsApp-first portal (records, photos, sessions remaining) to own the patient relationship.

finding: Independent reviews are almost non-existent. The only Capterra review is one star, titled 'Worst app ever'.
public_reaction: "Worst app ever" (1-star, Capterra)
our_action: Earn early social proof on Capterra and G2 from design-partner clinics. Eka's weak public review base leaves room.

finding: A competitor comparison (MocDoc) says Eka focuses on clinical data and interoperability, with simpler OP-oriented billing.
our_action: Show off Clinozy's ledger, credits, packages and daily cash close, all things Eka lacks for procedure-heavy clinics.

finding: Eka has no visible in-house pharmacy, stock, machine booking or aesthetic package module. It is positioned as an EMR and ABDM platform.
our_action: Position Clinozy against Eka: 'EMR is 10% of running a skin clinic.'

finding: A free doctor app plus a consumer PHR creates a two-sided network.
psychology: Freemium plus network effects: free entry removes risk (zero-price effect), and patient records on the PHR create switching costs and data lock-in.
our_action: Beat it: offer free data export and ABHA interoperability ('your data is yours'), which neutralises lock-in fears and turns Eka's moat into Clinozy's trust message.

finding: The AI scribe sells relief from documentation burden.
psychology: Effort reduction and novelty: doctors adopt tools that remove typing. The 'magic moment' in the first consult drives word of mouth among doctors.
our_action: Beat it: put AI where aesthetics revenue is, such as auto-drafting a treatment plan and package quote from the consult and sending it on WhatsApp. That ties time saved to money earned.

finding: The 'first ABDM-approved private platform' claim borrows government authority.
psychology: Authority bias: government badges reduce perceived risk for conservative doctor buyers.
our_action: Get ABDM certification early and display it next to GST, DPDP compliance and audit-log badges.

finding: AestheticsPro is built around treatment packages, memberships, subscriptions and 'client banks' (prepaid credit), plus injectable and product inventory.
our_action: Clinozy has packages and offers but no memberships, subscriptions or wallet credit. Add recurring memberships and prepaid wallet balances.

finding: AestheticsPro is well liked overall, at about 4.4–4.5/5 on Capterra from roughly 516–658 reviews. Reviewers cite an intuitive interface and good support staff.
public_reaction: Summary praises an 'intuitive and simple' interface and helpful support.
our_action: A large review base is its moat. Clinozy should aim for 50+ reviews in year one through review-request automation.

finding: AestheticsPro offers online 'Book Now' booking, a client portal and automated reminders.
our_action: Clinozy needs public online booking with doctor, room and machine availability. Its machine-aware scheduling is a differentiator to show in booking.

finding: The Executive tier and above includes a client portal, subscriptions and memberships, with marketing tools in the higher tiers.
our_action: Plan Clinozy's portal and membership features as one tier upgrade, but don't hide basic reminders behind it.

finding: Texting, video visits and e-prescriptions need third-party accounts connected to AestheticsPro, and e-Rx costs extra.
public_reaction: "Texting, video visits, and prescriptions require third party integration that needs the client to set up separate accounts then connect to AP."
our_action: Build WhatsApp, prescriptions and payments natively. Message: 'No extra accounts, it's all in Clinozy.'

finding: Support is ticket-only with no live phone or chat.
public_reaction: "I could never talk first hand (or even chat) with someone. I would have to submit a ticket, wait for a response..."
our_action: Offer live WhatsApp chat support. It's a cheap differentiator in India.

finding: Capterra's summary flags frequent glitches and outages.
public_reaction: Summary con: 'frequent glitches and outages'.
our_action: Publish a status page and uptime SLA, and add offline-tolerant PWA caching for the Today board so the front desk never stops.

finding: Pricing is confusing: 'starting at $59' on the vendor site versus $75/user Professional, $160 Pro-Plus (2 users, +$85/user) and $285 Executive elsewhere, plus unexpected fees and costly custom documents.
public_reaction: Reviewers report unexpected fees and that it was costly to add new documents for new services.
our_action: Simple, all-inclusive INR pricing with unlimited consent and form templates.

finding: Scheduling limits: users couldn't create separate calendars for in-office and out-of-office clients, and it didn't scale as services grew.
public_reaction: "Good for getting started, but as I added services it wasn't quite up to what I needed."
our_action: Use Clinozy's room, machine and doctor resource scheduling with branch-level calendars, and market 'scales from 1 chair to 10 branches'.

finding: AestheticsPro is US-centric, with no GST invoices, INR, WhatsApp or Indian pharmacy rules.
our_action: Indian aesthetic chains looking at global tools hit this wall. Clinozy should market 'global aesthetic depth, Indian compliance'.

finding: Memberships and client banks lock in prepaid value.
psychology: Endowment effect and sunk cost: prepaid credit feels like 'my money at the clinic', which drives return visits. Recurring billing makes churn take effort (default bias).
our_action: Beat it: show remaining wallet and package balance on every WhatsApp reminder ('₹4,500 and 3 sessions waiting for you'), and add expiry nudges. That makes the endowment salient, which AestheticsPro's portal doesn't do proactively.

finding: Automated reminders and online booking reduce no-shows.
psychology: Commitment and consistency: self-booked appointments create a public commitment, and reminders exploit implementation intentions.
our_action: Beat it: add a confirm/reschedule reply on WhatsApp plus an optional no-show deposit via UPI (loss aversion). Deposits are far more effective than SMS reminders alone.

finding: Tiered plans hide memberships and portal features in Executive.
psychology: Decoy and upsell ladder: the middle tier anchors, and the features clinics need most (memberships) push upgrades.
our_action: Avoid a resentment-inducing feature hostage. Put revenue features like memberships in the core plan, and charge per branch for scale instead.

finding: Moxie is a 'business-in-a-box' for US medspas: an EHR/POS suite plus coaching, discounted supplies and help launching a practice.
our_action: Clinozy can't copy the full service model pre-launch, but a 'Launch your clinic' playbook (price list templates, package templates, consent forms) captures part of the value.

finding: Each practice gets a dedicated practice success manager, and job listings suggest each manager handles about 50 practices.
public_reaction: Moxie testimonial: "held my hand from day 1" (vendor-curated).
our_action: For premium chains, offer a named success manager. For everyone else, use a growth checklist in-app.

finding: Moxie pushes clinic-branded memberships and packages to raise revenue and average order value, plus 'beauty bank' credits.
our_action: Gap: build memberships and prepaid credit in Clinozy Offerings, with revenue reporting on deferred package liability.

finding: Moxie runs marketing for clients (Meta ads, local SEO, promotions) and claims 8x Meta ROI by year one.
public_reaction: Case studies cite '130+ 5-Star Reviews' and '+18% average order value' (self-reported).
our_action: Clinozy has a Marketing role but no campaigns. Add WhatsApp broadcast campaigns, review requests and ad lead ingestion (Meta lead forms into Leads).

finding: A Series B of $10M came with a 'Compliance Defender' product and AmSpa platinum vendor status.
our_action: Compliance is a selling point. Clinozy should package consent, audit log and prescription-rule features as 'Compliance' for Indian regulations (DPDP, Drugs and Cosmetics Act records).

finding: An AI assistant ('MAIA') handles inventory and supply ordering, with VIP pricing on injectables through Moxie's supply arm.
our_action: Clinozy's stock runway can add auto-drafted purchase orders and group-buying deals with suppliers and MRs, creating a marketplace revenue line.

finding: Moxie offers automated messaging to reduce no-shows plus a client CRM and POS-style checkout.
our_action: Clinozy has Tasks automation. Add no-show prediction and deposit rules.

finding: Pricing isn't published and requires a sales call. Some directories describe a bundle of services, so fees may scale beyond software.
our_action: Message: 'Software you own, at a price you can see. No coaching retainers.' Clinic owners in India are price-sensitive and wary of revenue-share models.

finding: There are almost no independent reviews (none found on Reddit, Trustpilot or BBB). Social proof is vendor-curated.
our_action: Clinozy should earn third-party reviews. Independent proof beats curated case studies with sceptical buyers.

finding: Moxie is US-only (US medspa regulations, US banking), with no India presence, GST or WhatsApp.
our_action: No direct competition in India. Borrow Moxie's 'growth partner' narrative for Indian aesthetic entrepreneurs, especially first-time clinic founders.

finding: Coaching plus a success manager sells identity and reassurance to first-time owners.
psychology: Identity and status ('aesthetic entrepreneur') plus fear of failure: a coach lowers perceived risk, and monthly coaching sessions create accountability (commitment).
our_action: Beat it: give owners a weekly 'Clinic Pulse' WhatsApp report with benchmarks against similar clinics. That offers the accountability of coaching without the retainer.

finding: Memberships are pitched for recurring revenue and higher order value.
psychology: Subscription inertia (default bias) and the endowment effect: members feel they are 'wasting' benefits if they don't visit, so their visit frequency rises.
our_action: Beat it: monthly 'unused benefits' nudges on WhatsApp, member-only offer slots (scarcity) and automatic renewals with UPI Autopay.

finding: Review generation ('130+ 5-star reviews') drives local search ranking and patient trust.
psychology: Social proof: patients choosing aesthetic providers rely on star counts. Asking right after a visible result raises response rates (peak-end rule).
our_action: Beat it: trigger the Google review request after the before/after reveal or the final package session, not at checkout, and route unhappy patients to a feedback call task instead.
